Use an affine change of coordinates, which preserves midpoints and volume ratios. Let the prism have bottom vertices
\[
A=(0,0,0),\quad B=(1,0,0),\quad C=(0,1,0),
\]
and top vertices
\[
A'=(0,0,1),\quad B'=(1,0,1),\quad C'=(0,1,1).
\]
The marked midpoints are then
\[
M=\left(\tfrac12,0,0\right)\quad\text{on }AB,
\]
\[
N=\left(0,\tfrac12,0\right)\quad\text{on }AC,
\]
and
\[
R=\left(\tfrac12,\tfrac12,1\right)\quad\text{on }B'C'.
\]

The cutting plane through \(M,N,R\) has equation
\[
2x+2y-z=1.
\]
At \(A=(0,0,0)\), the quantity \(2x+2y-z-1=-1<0\), so the part containing \(A\) satisfies
\[
z\ge 2x+2y-1.
\]

At a fixed height \(z\), the full cross-section is the triangle
\[
x\ge0,\quad y\ge0,\quad x+y\le1,
\]
while the part containing \(A\) is
\[
x+y\le \frac{z+1}{2}.
\]
This smaller triangle is similar to the full triangle with linear scale
\[
\frac{z+1}{2},
\]
so its area is
\[
\left(\frac{z+1}{2}\right)^2
\]
of the full cross-sectional area.

Thus the fraction of the prism in the part containing \(A\) is
\[
\int_0^1 \left(\frac{z+1}{2}\right)^2\,dz
=
\frac14\int_0^1 (z+1)^2\,dz
=
\frac14\cdot\frac{7}{3}
=
\frac{7}{12}.
\]
Therefore the desired volume is
\[
504\cdot\frac{7}{12}=42\cdot 7=294.
\]
